diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The following result is a stronger version of the sampling inequality 
(see, e.g., Wendland and Rieger \cite{wen-rie:2005}).  
For a proof we refer to \cite{nak:2017b}.

\max_{|\alpha|_1\le 3}\sup_{x\in (-R,R)^d}|D^{\alpha}v^h(t_k,x)| 
\le C\max_{|\alpha|_1\le 3}\sup_{x\in (-R,R)^d}|D^{\alpha}v^h(t_n,x)| 
\le C\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}^d}|f(x)|.  
Here we have used Lemma \ref{lem:4.8} again to derive the last inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.8 asserts that for any grid function g and all multi-indices with |alpha|_1 <= 3, the derivative D^alpha I(g) on (-R, R)^d is bounded by C max_j |g(x^{(j)})| with C independent of h. This is mathematically impossible for |alpha|_1 >= 1. By definition, I(g) interpolates g on Gamma. For any two closest points x^{(i)}, x^{(j)} in Gamma with |x^{(i)} - x^{(j)}| = 2 Delta_2 x, choosing g such that g(x^{(i)}) = 1 and g(x^{(j)}) = -1 yields, by the Mean Value Theorem along the segment between x^{(i)} and x^{(j)}, a point xi where |D I(g)(xi)| >= 2 / (2 Delta_2 x) = 1 / Delta_2 x. Since Delta_2 x -> 0 as h -> 0, sup_{x} |D I(g)(x)| -> infinity, directly contradicting the claimed uniform bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish stability and convergence of the kernel collocation scheme without asserting uniform bounds on interpolant derivatives of arbitrary grid data, which would require an entirely new proof architecture.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.9 crucially relies on Lemma 4.8 to establish uniform C^3 bounds on v^h(t_k, ·), and Lemma 4.10 uses Lemma 4.8 to bound interpolation error for Lipschitz functions. Because Lemma 4.8 is false, the stability results in Lemma 4.9 and the main convergence result in Theorem 4.5 are left unsupported.
issues.title: False stability bound on derivatives of the interpolation operator
issues.why_classification: Lemma 4.8 is mathematically false by the Mean Value Theorem, and the paper's central theorem (Theorem 4.5) depends entirely on the stability bounds derived from it. No source-supported resolution is available to recover convergence without a fundamental reconstruction of the proofs.
